checks.check: Authenticate retained corrected base and repack all new records in memory
Execute unmodified fixture_disk_identity function under host BusyBox sh using inherited anonymous memory file descriptors

limitations: No guest boot, KVM invocation, SSH session, block-device mutation or hardware validation was performed.

Host software checks and anonymous-file identity-function tests do not prove physical boot, 24-hour workload behavior, actual CPU allocation, KVM acceleration, network transfer, media health, thermal performance or zero physical SD writes.

Enrollment must authenticate kernel and disposable fixture seed, preserve counter-3 backup, and establish four vCPUs/KVM. Release acceptance additionally needs external network transfers, cycle progression, host telemetry/error evidence and normal service/QEMU shutdown.
Hash verification after sync can use the guest page cache; the documentation correctly discloses this limitation.
review_findings: The producer authenticates compressed input before decompression, bounds archive size, changes only init plus two new records, and permits only fresh private direct out directories.

Guest disk writes follow PID 1 and exact QEMU virt compatible guard, exact vda size and ext4 identity, ro,noload mount and fixture marker/counter checks. No physical host disk scan or formatting path exists.
The bounded scratch name is unlinked before creation; counter symlinks are rejected. Routine workload writes target only guest counter and scratch; tmpfs contains bounded payload and status.

Release mode is fixed to 86400 monotonic uptime seconds; smoke mode is explicitly separate. CPU workers hash and verify the RAM payload, publish atomic heartbeats, and must remain alive and progress; scratch writes are synced and verified.
Cleanup must sync and unmount before PASS; failure markers are emitted on checked failures. Collector must reject every failure marker and verify guest-initiated shutdown independently.
HTTP status rejects POST and query input; network throughput and hash transfer are explicitly external collector duties, rather than inferred from httpd liveness.

passed_review_points: Fixed JSON service argument is shell-safe after restrictive service-name validation; validated IPv4 cannot add SSH options.
Strict host-key policy and fixed host-key alias are present; no trust enrollment performed.
Frame size, exact payload length, finite JSON, payload hash and transport failure checks fail closed.
Actual KVM descriptors include exact vendor VGIC label, four vCPU descriptors, VM descriptor; UID/GID/capability/NoNewPrivs restrictions enforced.
SD write/discard/flush counters and direct mounts fail; thermal critical trips are required and exceeded trips fail.
HTTP redirects/proxies disabled; actual payload traverses SSH to workstation without payload files.
CPU helper refuses root, uses RAM and four forked workers, detects early exits, terminates/reaps remaining workers with bounded SIGKILL fallback.
Smoke/release durations remain distinct; no path grants hardware acceptance; inactive/completed collection exits pending external completion.
SMART explicitly unproved and physical/console/exit/duration acceptance delegated to coordinator.
limits: No SSH or hardware operation performed.
No actual 24-hour execution or installed-host acceptance.
Independent review covers only the four named source/test/documentation files; coordinator retains integration and hardware acceptance.

resolved_findings.evidence: Only -m 256/256M accepted. Remote systemctl show collects MemoryMax; validate requires string 536870912. Negative tests reject 512/512M and missing, unlimited or incorrect limits.

Main loop invokes ProgressWatchdog after successful running-sample validation. Both elapsed_seconds and cycles independently require advancement within 120 collector-monotonic seconds. Tests accept exactly 120 seconds and reject longer stalls even while the other counter advances. disk_counter correctly remains a per-run identity; prior review suggestion to require its progress was superseded by clarified interface.
Every error-bearing validated sample gets nvme_kernel_error_assessment=coordinator_review_required. Empty baseline gets no_errors_observed; changed error sets still fail. Tests cover all three cases.

Validation/watchdog failure retains the decoded bounded sample. data resets to None before every probe; later transport failure therefore cannot relabel the previous sample. Recording regressions cover both cases.

advisories.finding: The phrase supplied identity exclusively overstates IdentitiesOnly=yes: OpenSSH can also use IdentityFile entries from inherited user/client configuration.
advisories.suggested_change: Remove exclusively, or intentionally isolate configuration if exclusive identity selection is required.
